page.layout: One column of dictionary entries, Hebrew and Latin. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. One catchword at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: גור m. Catulus, Genes.49.9. Deuter.33.22. Plural. cum Aff. גוריה Catulos suos, Ezech.19.2.
גור m. Idem: Plur. Constr. כגורי Sicut catuli, Jer.51. v.18. Et fœm. cum Aff. גרתיו [?] Catulis suis, Nah.2.12.

גֵר m. Peregrinus, Inquilinus, Advena, Accola: Aff. וגרך Et peregrinus tuus, Exod.20.10. Plur. גרים Peregrini Exod.22.21. R.Sal. Exod.22.20. גר אדם שלא נולד באותה מדינה אלא בא מִדינָה אַחֶרֶת לָגוּר שָׁם [?] Ger est homo, qui non natus est in illa civitate, sed venit ex alia civitate ad habitandum illic.
מָגוֹר m. Formido, Metus, Pavor, Jer.6.25. Fœmin. מְגוּרָה; unde Constructi. מְגוֹרַת רָשָׁע Formido improbi, Prov.10.24.

מָגוּר m. Commoratio, Habitatio, Formido: Aff. בְּמְגוּרָם In commoratione ipsorum, Psal.55.16. Plural. Constr. מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו [?] Peregrinationum patris sui, Gen.37.1. Aff. בְּמְגוּרָיו In habitationibus suis, Job.18.19. מְגוּרַי Formidines meas, Thren.2.22. Vide & מָגַר.

מְגוּרָה f. Granarium, Horreum, quia fruges in eo congregantur & recipiuntur, Hag.2.20. Item Formido, unde Plur. מְגוּרֹתָם Formidines eorū, Jesa.66.4. וּמִכָּל־מְגוּרֹתַי Et ex omnibus pavoribus meis, Psal.34.5.
מַמְגּוּרוֹת f.p. Granaria, Joel.1.17. Vox anomala, inquit Aben Esra, aucta duplici מ formativo.
נוּשׁ m. Strigmentum, Ramentum, Pulvis: וְנוּשׁ Et ramentum, Job.7.5. scribitur cum ʼ [?] & legitur per ו. Apud Talmudicos, גּוּר אֲגוּשָׁא Condemnatus ad pulverem.
גִּזְבָּר m. Chald. Quæstor, Præfectus ærario, Esr.1.8. Plural. ex aliâ formâ, גִּזְבְּרַיָּא Quæstores, Esræ 7.21.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points are read from a low-resolution scan and may be incomplete. Points marked [?] are doubtful. "Jer.51" is printed as an old-style numeral that may read 5I or 51. "frages" may be "fruges" with a long s. "Jesa" may be "Iesa". The Aramaic-looking form in the entry for נוּשׁ and the apostrophe after "cum" are not fully clear. The Hebrew letter after "per" resembles the numeral 1 but is read as ו. The large headword initials נוש and גזבר are set in larger Hebrew type and are transcribed as ordinary headwords.
